Encore points, 0.2 cents each, 500 points = $1 redeemable only at Gap Inc. brands or the Encore Market, no cash option; replaced Navyist Rewards and Good Rewards in February 2026); priceline-points (Priceline VIP Rewards points, 1.0 cent each as statement credits against Priceline purchases, gift cards or merchandise, so effectively cash with a 1.0 cent cash option); emirates-skywards (Emirates Skywards Miles, about 1.0 cent per mile per NerdWallet October 2026, no cash option); breeze-points (BreezePoints, fixed 1.0 cent toward Breeze fares and fees, no cash option). Existing program valuations for reference: delta-skymiles 1.2 cents, hilton-honors 0.4, marriott-bonvoy 0.75, jetblue-trueblue 1.35 to 1.4, american-aadvantage 1.45 to 1.7 (TPG and NerdWallet October 2026).

Amex business category mapping: select-merchants stands for U.S. shipping providers, U.S. advertising in select media, U.S. office supply stores and single purchases of $5,000 or more; phone stands for wireless telephone services purchased directly from U.S. providers; transit stands for Amex's transit category (taxicabs, rideshare, trains, tolls, parking). Delta Gold Business has two separate $50,000 caps (shipping, advertising); Delta Platinum Business has one $100,000 cap shared across transit, shipping and large purchases. Labels on earn rules carry the issuer wording.

Amex base caps the schema cannot model: Hilton Honors Business base 5 drops to 3 after $100,000 of purchases per calendar year; Delta Reserve Business base rises to 1.5 on all purchases after $150,000 in a calendar year.

Amex Plum Card: discontinued for new applicants in April 2026 (Doctor of Credit, April 10, 2026) when the Graphite Business Cash Unlimited launched. It earns no points or cash back; base is 0 and the 1.5% early pay discount is described in tips. Included for existing holders with medium confidence.

Amazon Business Prime American Express Card: closed to new applicants in spring 2026; Amazon moved both business cards to U.S. Bank (Mastercard) on May 13, 2026 for new applicants and replaced Amex accounts from August 14, 2026. The Amex entry records the legacy Amex earning (5% or 90-day terms on Amazon, AWS and Whole Foods up to $120,000, 2% dining, gas and wireless) with program amazon-points at 1 cent per point. The U.S. Bank Prime Business Card terms (5% Amazon up to $150,000, 5% U.S. Bank Travel Center, 2% on the top three eligible categories each cycle up to $150,000, 1% elsewhere, no fees) are described in tips so the merge step can add a us-bank card if wanted.

Lowe's Business Rewards Card from American Express: Amex still hosts the product and member pages, but Nav reports it stopped taking applications in April 2026, the same month Synchrony launched the MyLowe's Pro Rewards American Express Card (April 30, 2026, Amex network, Synchrony issuer, no annual fee, 2 points per dollar at dining, office supply and wireless merchants, 1 point elsewhere, Lowe's points by Pro status tier). Included for existing holders with medium confidence; program is cashback because Lowe's Business Rewards points redeem at 1 cent as statement credits.

Barclays AAdvantage Aviator Red, Silver and Business: closed to new applicants October 1, 2025 and transferred to Citi on April 24, 2026 (Red to Citi AAdvantage Platinum Select, Silver to Citi AAdvantage Globe, Business to Citi AAdvantage Business World Elite, Blue to Citi AAdvantage Gold, base Aviator to AAdvantage MileUp). Barclays no longer issues or services any AAdvantage card. The three entries are kept as historical records with their pre-conversion earning so a tool can explain the conversion; the merge step may drop them or point holders at the Citi entries. Aviator Business is low confidence because no issuer page could be read.

Hawaiian Airlines World Elite Mastercard: Barclays removed it from its own site on October 1, 2025 but still issues it as the Hawaiian Airlines Bank of Hawaii World Elite Mastercard through Bank of Hawaii and inflight applications (Frequent Miler July 2026, Your Mileage May Vary October 1, 2026). It now earns Alaska Atmos Rewards points. Alaska and Bank of America announced on April 20, 2026 that Bank of America will become the sole Atmos card issuer, with no conversion date or target card published. A Hawaiian Airlines Business World Elite Mastercard ($99) also exists and was not modeled.

Wyndham: Barclays and Wyndham refreshed the lineup on June 17, 2026 (Earner $0 with 3X dining, groceries, gas and EV; Earner Plus $95 with 4X dining, groceries and travel; Earner Business $149 with 5X gas, EV, marketing, advertising, office supply and shipping and a 20% award discount; new Earner Premier $395 with 8X Wyndham, 4X dining, groceries and travel, 25% award discount, 30,000 anniversary points and about $400 in credits). Existing holders keep the old fees and earning until they upgrade; both versions are described in each card's watchOut. The Earner Premier was outside the assignment and is not modeled. Barclays' own product pages still show the pre-refresh wording. Travel on the Plus is expanded into travel, gas, ev-charging, transit and rental-car rules at the same rate for matching; hotels other than Wyndham earn 1X.

Carnival: the Carnival World Mastercard (2X Carnival, 1X elsewhere, FunPoints) was replaced on September 1, 2026 by the Carnival Rewards Mastercard (3X Carnival, 2X restaurants and grocery stores, 1X elsewhere, 1 Status Qualifying Star per dollar); existing accounts migrated in September 2026 and FunPoints converted 1 to 1. The entry models the new card under id barclays-carnival-rewards-mastercard.

Old Navy and Gap: Gap Inc. replaced Navyist Rewards and Good Rewards with Encore on February 24, 2026. The Barclays cards are now the Old Navy Encore Mastercard and Gap Encore Mastercard (Barclays' list still says Gap Good Rewards Mastercard; the Athleta Rewards Mastercard and Banana Republic card are the same product). Store-only Encore Credit Cards earn only at Gap Inc. brands and are described in tips rather than modeled. Rates are recorded in points (25, 15, 5 per dollar at 0.2 cents each) so base is 5, not 1; a tool should convert with the program value. World and World Elite accounts earn 10 points per dollar on the base.

Priceline VIP Rewards Visa: still offered through Priceline (Frequent Miler shows a 20,000 point offer and an expired September 2026 offer) but absent from Barclays' public list; the grandfathered Priceline Rewards Visa was converted into it on July 2, 2025. Medium confidence.

Breeze Easy Visa exists and is on Barclays' card list ($89, Visa Signature); modeled with program breeze-points. Emirates Skywards Rewards World Elite Mastercard ($99, same earning, Silver status) exists alongside the Premium and is described in the Premium entry's tips rather than modeled.

Barclays protections: Barclays removed extended warranty, purchase protection, price protection, return protection and trip delay from all its cards on November 1, 2019, so purchaseProtection, extendedWarranty and tripDelay are false on every Barclays card. Cell phone protection and secondary rental car coverage are confirmed for the JetBlue Plus (World Elite guide via HelloSafe and Upgraded Points) and set on the Premier and Aviator World Elite cards; where no source names them for a card the keys are omitted. Barclays does not publish card-specific guides to benefits on its public pages.
Non-schema fields used: label (issuer wording on earn rules) and unsure. Duplicate select-merchants rules on one card (Delta Gold Business) carry separate caps and are distinguished by label.

Welcome offers in tips are current as of October 28, 2026 and change often: Delta business offers end November 4, 2026; Hilton Business ends January 13, 2027; Marriott Business ends November 4, 2026; Emirates runs through January 5, 2027.

Membership Rewards values: statement credit cash-out is about 0.6 cents per point; flights booked through Amex Travel redeem at 1 cent per point; other Amex Travel bookings run about 0.7 cents; transfer partners (airline and hotel programs) are where the value is, with typical estimates of 1.3 to 2 cents per point depending on the redemption
Blue Cash cards and Cash Magnet pay cash back as Reward Dollars; 1 Reward Dollar equals $1 as a statement credit or at Amazon checkout, so cash back rates are plain percentages
American Express is not accepted at Costco warehouses, Costco gas stations or Costco.com; the warehouse category never applies to these cards at Costco

Amex defines U.S. supermarkets to exclude superstores (Walmart, Target), warehouse clubs, convenience stores, specialty food stores and meal-kit services; U.S. gas stations exclude gas sold by supermarkets, superstores and warehouse clubs; these exclusions apply to every Amex card with those categories

Blue Business Plus and Blue Business Cash: the base rate of 2 applies to the first $50,000 of purchases per calendar year, then 1; the schema has no base cap field so the cap is described in tips and watchOut
Marriott Bonvoy Bevy: the $15,000 per year cap on 4X is combined across the dining and groceries rules, not separate

Business Gold: the choice object models Amex picking the top two categories automatically each billing cycle; the holder does not choose; select-merchants stands for both U.S. advertising in online, TV and radio media and U.S. electronic goods retailers and software and cloud providers; the $150,000 cap is combined across the 4X categories

Business Platinum: home-improvement stands for Amex's U.S. construction material and hardware suppliers category; select-merchants stands for U.S. electronic goods retailers, software and cloud providers, and shipping providers; the $2,000,000 cap is combined, and single purchases of $5,000 or more also earn 2X
Gold: the portal-travel rate of 5 is for prepaid hotels through Amex Travel only; flights through Amex Travel earn 3 and prepaid car rentals or cruises through Amex Travel earn 2

Platinum and Business Platinum: portal-travel 5 covers flights (Platinum only) and prepaid hotels through Amex Travel, and prepaid Airbnb bookings through Amex Travel since October 22, 2026; other Membership Rewards cards earn 2 on prepaid Airbnb through Amex Travel

Classic Green, Amex EveryDay, Amex EveryDay Preferred and Cash Magnet are closed to new applicants (Green since July 2026, the others since September 2024) but still widely held and still in Amex's cardmember agreements, so they are included with medium confidence
No new merchant ids were added; all merchant rules use delta, hilton, marriott, amex-travel, netflix and spotify from the schema list

Sources: Amex product pages, the Amex rewards-info category definition pages (retail, travel, business), and the Amex benefit policy eligible-card pages were used first; NerdWallet, The Points Guy, Doctor of Credit, AwardWallet, Upgraded Points, InsideFlyer, Frequent Miler and Delta's newsroom filled gaps where Amex pages were removed or did not render

Issuer values outside the schema enum: Navy Federal, USAA, PenFed, Alliant, SoFi, Robinhood, Upgrade and WebBank (Petal 2), as the assignment directed short institution names; the merge step may remap WebBank to 'other'.

Navy Federal: Flagship Rewards closed to new applicants September 10, 2026 and was replaced by Flagship Premier ($95, 4x travel, 3x dining, 1x other, $100 airline credit, no Amazon Prime); the old card is included for existing holders with medium confidence. nRewards Secured is now sold as cashRewards Secured (1%). cashRewards network is Visa or Mastercard by applicant choice; Visa is recorded. The 1.75% direct deposit tier ended October 6, 2024. Membership is required for every Navy Federal card.

USAA: usaa.com product pages require cookies and would not render, but the rewards terms pages at usaa.com/banking/terms/ did for Preferred Cash, Eagle Navigator and Eagle Adapt. USAA launched Eagle Adapt (Visa, 3% on eight categories up to $3,000 per quarter combined) and Eagle Ascend (Amex, 2% on the top eligible category each month, automatic) on July 15, 2026 and refreshed Cashback Rewards Plus (separate 5% gas and 5% military base caps, groceries up to 3%, 0% foreign fee). The older USAA Rewards American Express and Rewards Visa Signature are no longer offered and are left out. Eagle Adapt's health and wellness category is mapped to drugstore plus fitness, and Eagle Ascend uses a choice object with a non-schema automatic flag.

PenFed: product pages render fee and multiplier numbers client-side, so figures were cross-checked with NerdWallet and the PenFed Honors Advantage page. Pathfinder lost its Honors Advantage annual fee waiver on September 28, 2026; everyone now pays $95. Power Cash is 1.5% base and 2% with Honors Advantage (military service or qualifying PenFed checking); the merge step may model Honors Advantage as an optional base override of 2 and an extra 1x on Pathfinder travel and dining. Defender Rewards (July 2026, 5x gas, 3x military stores and sporting goods) was added although not in the assignment. Anyone can join PenFed.

Alliant: the 2.5% tier ended November 1, 2025 and the card is a flat 1.5% for everyone; 90 days of membership are required before applying. SoFi: the Unlimited 2% card is invitation based and pays 1 cent only into SoFi products; Everyday Cash Rewards (3% dining, 2% groceries) was added; the SoFi Essential card (3% only on SoFi Travel, no other rewards) is left out as a credit-builder with effectively no earning. Robinhood Gold Card: 3% everything, 5% portal travel, requires Robinhood Gold ($50 per year); 3% foreign transaction fee for accounts opened on or after July 1, 2026 (fxFee recorded as 3; earlier accounts have 0). Statement credit redemption is 0.7 cent, so 1 cent requires depositing to the brokerage account.

Upgrade: upgrade.com/credit-cards was blocked from fetching; the help center pages for Cash Rewards and Triple Cash Rewards were used. Upgrade now markets OneCard Essentials (invitation and pre-approval, 3% gas, groceries, streaming and utilities, 1% other), which was added. Cash back on the Cash Rewards and Triple Cash cards is earned as you repay, not at purchase; the schema has no field for this so it is in tips. The standard Upgrade OneCard (3% on everyday categories capped at $500 per year, 2% or 1.5% base depending on a Rewards Checking account) is left out because its terms changed for accounts opened after April 6, 2026 and current terms are not published.

Petal 2: closed to new applicants; Petal cards were replaced by Tilt Engage, Tilt Motion and Tilt Essentials (WebBank) in August 2025. Included for existing holders with base 1 (starting tier) and tips explaining the 1.25% and 1.5% tiers after 6 and 12 consecutive on-time payments. X1 Card: left out; Robinhood cut X1 earning to 1.5x on November 21, 2025, eliminated boosts and invited holders to the Robinhood Gold Card, and X1 points were worth 1 cent only at select merchants, so it no longer has a published current rewards structure worth modeling.

Bank of America co-brands: bankofamerica.com product pages were blocked by the fetch tool, so reference sites dated October 2026 were used and are listed per card. Alaska Airlines Visa Signature and Alaska Business are now the Atmos Rewards Ascent Visa Signature ($95) and Atmos Rewards Visa Signature Business ($70 plus $25 per card) after the August 2025 Alaska and Hawaiian program merger; the Companion Fare now requires $6,000 in prior-year spend. Air France KLM moved from World Elite Mastercard to Visa Signature in March 2026 and added 3x dining with a 1.5x base. Royal Caribbean Visa Signature and Celebrity Visa Signature were replaced March 31, 2026 by Royal ONE ($0) and Royal ONE Plus ($99); old cardholders are being converted to Royal ONE, so the old cards are left out. Norwegian Cruise Line World Mastercard is unchanged. Free Spirit Travel More and Free Spirit Travel Mastercard are left out: Spirit Airlines ceased operations May 2, 2026 and Bank of America is converting those accounts to Customized Cash Rewards (keeping no foreign transaction fee) with Free Spirit points converting to Bank of America cash rewards. AAA Member Rewards Visa is left out: Bank of America discontinued it in 2022 and the current AAA cards are issued by Comenity (Bread).

Wells Fargo: Choice Privileges, Choice Privileges Select, One Key, Reflect and Signify Business Cash were confirmed on creditcards.wellsfargo.com. One Key+ has no product page on Wells Fargo's site as of October 28, 2026 and is included with medium confidence from NerdWallet, Upgraded Points and AwardWallet for existing holders. Wells Fargo bonus categories exclude purchases made through third-party payment accounts, online marketplaces, mobile card readers and digital wallets on the Choice cards; One Key cards exclude PayPal and supplier-billed charges.

U.S. Bank: usbank.com personal card pages for SKYPASS and LATAM returned errors; the SKYPASS cards use NerdWallet (October 9, 2026) and Frequent Miler with medium confidence because sources disagree on the Visa Signature fee ($95 vs $99) and whether the second 2x category is gas or restaurants. LATAM Pass is left out: U.S. Bank no longer issues it and LATAM's U.S. cards are now issued through Cardless. Business Altitude Power ($195, 2x everything, 2.5x mobile wallet up to $5,000 per quarter, 6x portal hotels and cars) is still shown on bizcards.usbank.com but not on the main business card page, so it is medium confidence. Business Altitude Connect's 4x cap of $150,000 per calendar year is combined across travel and gas. Harley-Davidson Visa Signature charges a 5% foreign transaction fee.

Discover: Discover it Secured closed to new applicants June 2, 2026 but is widely held and included; its 2% on gas and restaurants is capped at $1,000 combined per quarter and it does not use the rotating calendar. Discover it Business is left out: Discover no longer offers any business card to new applicants (the 1.5% card closed years ago).

Rule fields beyond the schema used here: label (issuer wording for select-merchants rules), walletPayOnly (Business Altitude Power mobile wallet rule), and choice.automatic (Eagle Ascend). No rules use until or afterRate.

Fetch blocks encountered: bankofamerica.com product pages (Alaska, Alaska Business, Air France KLM), robinhood.com/creditcard/ (the non-trailing-slash URL worked), upgrade.com/credit-cards/, usaa.com product pages (cookie wall), usbank.com SKYPASS and LATAM pages, nerdwallet.com Eagle Navigator and PenFed Power Cash reviews, bankrate.com PenFed Power Cash review.

Capital One Walmart Rewards Mastercard is left out: Capital One stopped accepting applications in 2024 and converted existing accounts to Quicksilver; Walmart's current card is the OnePay CashRewards card from Synchrony.

Capital One Spark Miles no longer exists under that name. On April 14, 2026 Capital One renamed Spark Miles to Venture Business ($95, 2X everything, 5X Capital One Business Travel) and Spark Miles Select to VentureOne Business ($0, 1.5X). The entry capital-one-venture-business covers the former Spark Miles; the old Spark Miles URL now redirects to the Venture Business page.

Capital One business card names as sold today are Spark 2% Cash Plus, Spark 2% Cash, Spark 1.5% Cash Select, Spark 1% Classic, Venture X Business, Venture Business and VentureOne Business. Only Spark Cash Plus, Spark Cash Select and Venture Business (ex Spark Miles) were in scope.

Capital One miles value: 1 cent per mile when redeemed for travel through Capital One Travel or as a statement credit against a travel purchase (within 90 days of posting). A check or non-travel statement credit pays about 0.5 cents per mile with a 5,000 mile minimum. Gift cards are about 1 cent. Transfers to 15+ airline and hotel partners (most at 1:1, some 2:1.5 or 5:3) are where the value is; The Points Guy valued miles at 1.85 cents in September 2026. Cash back cards (Savor, Quicksilver, Spark Cash) redeem at face value.

Capital One network changes: after closing the Discover acquisition in May 2025, Capital One began originating some new Venture, VentureOne, Savor and Quicksilver accounts on the Discover network in early 2026. In April 2026 it notified a subset of existing Quicksilver and QuicksilverOne holders that their cards move to Discover and gain 3% at grocery stores and gas stations. The cards as advertised on capitalone.com still show the flat 1.5%. Venture X, business and cobranded cards were not affected. Network values in this file reflect the historical default (Mastercard for the consumer cards other than Venture X); a tool should treat network as per-account for Capital One consumer cards.

Citi Custom Cash was closed to new applications on May 28, 2026. It is included because it is widely held and the earning rules are unchanged for existing holders. The choice object uses capPeriod 'month' to mean per billing cycle and includes a non-schema 'automatic': true flag because the top category is chosen by Citi, not the holder.

Citi Rewards+ no longer exists. It was converted to the no-annual-fee Citi Strata Card on July 20, 2025 and the round-up and 10% points-back grandfathering ended July 19, 2026. The entry citi-strata covers it. Citi Strata's self-select options include cosmetic stores, barber shops, hair salons and pet supply stores, which have no category id; they are mapped to select-merchants and explained in tips.

Citi protections: Citi removed purchase protection, extended warranty, price protection, trip delay and most other shopping and travel protections from consumer cards in September 2019. Since then it restored a 24-month extended warranty on Double Cash, Custom Cash, Strata Premier and Rewards+ (now Strata) in November 2024; Strata Premier (2024 relaunch) and Strata Elite (July 2025 launch) carry a full set of travel protections plus purchase protection; the Costco card keeps Damage and Theft Purchase Protection and Worldwide Car Rental Insurance. The AAdvantage Platinum Select and Simplicity pages list no protections.

Citi ThankYou transfers: points from Double Cash, Custom Cash and Strata transfer to the full partner list only at a reduced ratio (about 30% less) unless the holder also has a Strata Premier or Strata Elite.

Costco Anywhere Visa: Costco raised the Costco gas rate from 4% to 5% in January 2026; other gas and EV charging stays at 4%; both share one $7,000 per year cap. Costco US warehouses accept only Visa credit cards. Rewards come as a single annual certificate after the February statement.

Non-schema field used: 'merchantNote' on earn rules to explain portal-only or time-window conditions (Capital One Entertainment 8%/5%, Capital One Travel 10X vs 5X split, Citi Nights 6X). The merge step can drop or keep it.
Merchant ids used from the schema list: capital-one-travel, citi-travel, costco, costco-gas, american-airlines. No new merchant ids were added.

Issuer pages that would not render through fetch (client-side rendered): Citi Custom Cash product page, Citi Costco page at the old URL (the current URL https://www.citi.com/credit-cards/costco-anywhere-visa-card rendered), Capital One Venture X disclosures, Capital One Venture benefits page. New merchant ids used in this file: american-red-cross (Freedom Flex Q4 2026 donations), audible (Prime Visa and Amazon Visa 5%/3%), airbnb and vrbo (Sapphire Preferred 3x vacation rentals), air-canada (Aeroplan card 3x), disney-plus, hulu and espn (Disney Premier Visa 5% at DisneyPlus.com, Hulu.com and Stream.ESPN.com).

New program ids used in this file: aeroplan-points (Air Canada Aeroplan Card) and disney-rewards (Disney Premier Visa Card earns Disney Rewards Dollars, worth $1 each only toward Disney purchases or statement credits against Disney, Disney+, Hulu, ESPN and direct airline purchases; it is not plain cash back).
